name: blink
description: Build, change and publish real apps by chatting with Blink: a web or mobile app with a database, sign-in, a backend and hosting, published to a live URL.

interface.longDescription:
Blink turns a description into a working app, with a database, sign-in, a backend and hosting, and publishes it to a live link. You do it all from this conversation.

What you can do:
• Build an app by describing it: a client portal, a booking site, an internal dashboard, a landing page or a mobile app.
• Change it by asking: "add a dark mode toggle" or "let clients approve deliverables".
• Answer Blink's questions right in the chat when it needs a decision, like which kind of app or which look.
• See the finished app right in the chat, with a screenshot and what changed, then publish it to a live URL.
• Look inside any project: list your projects, read the source at any saved version, compare two versions, query the database, and read backend logs when something fails.
• Restore an earlier version if a change went wrong.

How it works: connecting is a normal sign-in, and you choose which Blink workspace to grant. Code changes always go through Blink's agent, so your app's source and its saved versions stay in step. You can disconnect at any time from Blink Settings, Access Tokens, Connected apps.
capabilities: Build and change apps by describing them
Answer the builder's questions in chat
Publish an app to a live URL
List projects with screenshots and status
Read source code at any saved version
defaultPrompt: Build me a client portal where clients log in and approve deliverables
Show my Blink projects and which ones are live
Check the backend logs of my app and tell me what's failing

positive.description: Shows which Blink workspace this connection can use.
positive.prompt: Which Blink workspace am I connected to?
positive.expected_behavior: Names the connected workspace (OpenAI's Blink) and the reviewer's role in it.

positive.description: Lists the workspace's projects in the projects card.
positive.expected_behavior: The projects card shows Habit Tracker and Recipe Box with their screenshots; Habit Tracker is marked Live.

positive.description: Builds a new app from a description and shows the result in the build card.
positive.prompt: Use Blink to build a one-page site for a coffee shop called Bean There, with its menu and opening hours.
positive.expected_behavior: A new project is created and the build card appears. If Blink asks a question, the card shows it as buttons and answering continues the build. The card ends with a screenshot of the site, what changed and the credits used.

positive.description: Reads the source of a project's latest saved version.
positive.prompt: List the source files of Habit Tracker, then show me the code of its main page.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists Habit Tracker's files (src/Shell.tsx, src/routes/index.tsx and more), then shows the main page's code (src/routes/index.tsx) from the latest saved version.

positive.description: Publishes a project to its live URL.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT asks to confirm, then Recipe Box is published and the reply gives its live URL. If the deploy is still running, it says so and confirms with blink_hosting_status.

negative.prompt: Show me the .env file of Habit Tracker.

negative.description: The plugin doesn't sell credits or plans.
The plugin can't delete a Blink account.

publication.release_notes: 1.1.2: Moves Blink to the new plugin package with a getting-started skill. Builds, publishes and restores now ask for confirmation, cards follow ChatGPT's look, and a remix lands in the connected workspace.
